deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the 1818 Göttingen meridian reductions. The previous page reduces α Lyrae; the next page reduces the right ascensions of γ Draconis using instrument constants m and n, with a constant change on 12/13 Sept. Here Gauss reduces the small zenith distances of γ Draconis, which culminates very close to the Göttingen zenith (dec ≈ +51°30′, latitude ≈ 51°32′). Such a star serves to control the zenith point and level of the meridian instrument.

Structure of each line: date | observed (instrument) zenith distance z_obs | correction r(t) | z_red = z_obs + r(t).

Side table (upper right): r(t) at 5-day intervals: Aug 23 +9.24, Aug 28 +9.91, Sep 2 +10.46, Sep 7 +10.92, Sep 12 +11.26, Sep 17 +11.46, Sep 22 +11.52. This is a smooth seasonal term. Its size (≈20″ annual range) and its stationary maximum near late September fit the aberration-dominated reduction of γ Dra's apparent declination to a mean place (Bradley's star); that physical reading is my inference. The second column of the main table is interpolated from this side table. For example, Aug 31: 9.91 + (3/5)(0.55) = 10.24; Sep 4: 10.46 + (2/5)(0.46) = 10.644 ≈ 10.64; Sep 10: 10.92 + (3/5)(0.34) = 11.124 ≈ 11.12. The values for Sep 15–20 (11.37, 11.46, 11.49) lie 0.01 below simple linear interpolation (11.38, 11.47, 11.50). The source of this ±0.01″ difference is unclear (rounding, or a finer table).

Group 1 (Aug 31 – Sep 12, 8 nights). The sums are 17.25+10.24=27.49, 20.97+10.35=31.32, 17.02+10.46=27.48, 19.35+10.64=29.99, 17.93+10.74=28.67, 16.03+10.83=26.86, 16.89+11.12=28.01, 18.53+11.26=29.79. The bracketed mean is 229.61/8 = 28.701 → 28″70.

A horizontal rule then marks an instrumental change after Sep 12. This matches the next page, where the constant n changes sign 'vom 13 Sept an'.

Group 2 (Sep 13 – Nov 10). The sums are 71.34+11.30=1′22.64, 71.70+11.34=1′23.04, 74.57+11.37=1′25.94, 74.29+11.46=1′25.75, 70.32+11.49=1′21.81, 75.02+11.51=1′26.53, Nov 3: 79.33+6.51=1′25.84, Nov 10: 80.85+4.71=1′25.56. The bracketed mean 1′24″51 equals the mean of the 7 values Sep 13 – Nov 3: 591.55/7 = 84.507″. Nov 10 is excluded; including it would give 84.64″, and the six September values alone give 84.29″.

'Mit der neuen Libelle' (with the new level). The same nights reduced with the new level give: Nov 3: 8′39.92+6.51 = 8′46.43; Nov 5: 8′40.36+5.99 = 8′46.35; Nov 10: 8′41.78+4.71 = 8′46.49. The new zero point is mutually very consistent (spread 0.14″).

December. Dec 4 is written with explicit signs: −6′52.47 − 2.46 = −6′54.93, written 6 54.94. Dec 16 and 18 are +8′44.98 and +8′48.62 with corrections −6.58 and −7.31. The correction must decrease smoothly: about −0.26″/day in November, reaching −6.58 on Dec 16. Hence Dec 1 and Dec 3 must also be negative (≈ −1.45, −2.12), and their zenith-distance entries 6′49.98 and 6′48.20 are almost certainly negative too, with signs omitted (my inference). The Dec 1–4 readings thus lie on the opposite side of the instrumental zero (probably a reversed instrument or circle position), while Dec 16–18 are positive. The values: Dec 1: −6′51.43; Dec 3: −6′50.32; Dec 4: −6′54.93(94); Dec 18: 8′48.62 − 7.31 = 8′41.31. For Dec 16, 8′44.98 − 6.58 = 8′38.40, but the page shows a corrected entry read as 8′4?.00 (47.00 overwritten with 41?). This does not agree with the arithmetic (see errors).

The faint pencil numbers '192' and '137' on the right are unexplained jottings.

Purpose: routine observatory reduction. Gauss brings successive meridian-instrument zenith distances of the near-zenith star γ Dra to a common epoch and forms night-means for each instrumental configuration (old level before and after the Sep 13 change, new level, December positions). These serve to monitor the instrument's zenith point. The companion page does the same for right ascension.
errors: Dec 4: 6′52.47 + 2.46 = 6′54.93, written 6′54.94 (0.01″ slip, or rounding from more decimals).

Dec 16: +8′44.98 − 6.58 = 8′38.40, but the result is written as 8′4?.00 (overwritten, read 47.00/41.00). Neither matches the arithmetic. Either the entry is misread or Gauss made a slip; the page itself shows a correction at this spot.
Interpolated corrections for Sep 15, 18, 20 (11.37, 11.46, 11.49) are 0.01″ below linear interpolation from the side table (11.38, 11.47, 11.50). This is negligible and possibly due to a finer table.
Signs of the Dec 1 and Dec 3 entries are omitted, though continuity of the correction shows they must be negative like Dec 4 (a notational omission, not a computational error).
The bracket on group 2 visually seems to span Sep 13–21, but the stated mean 1′24″51 corresponds to Sep 13 – Nov 3 (7 values).

results.what: Reduction of observed zenith distances of γ Draconis by linear interpolation in a 5-day table of seasonal (apparent-place) corrections, with nightly means per instrumental configuration
results.modern_name: Reduction to mean place / zenith-point determination of a meridian circle with a near-zenith star; linear table interpolation; arithmetic mean
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th–19th c. observatory practice (Bradley, Bessel, etc.)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely routine numerical reduction of meridian observations of γ Draconis at Göttingen in 1818: additions, linear interpolation, and averages. Nothing mathematically or historically novel.

checkable.asserts: Mean of the 8 reduced values Aug 31–Sep 12 equals 28.70125″ ≈ 28″70
Mean of the 7 reduced values Sep 13–Nov 3 equals 84.507″ = 1′24″51
Dec 16 reduced value should be 8′38.40 (expression equals 0), not 8′47.00 or 8′41.00
Dec 4 magnitude is 6′54.93 (expression equals 0), vs written 6′54.94
Dec 18 reduced value 8′41.31 is correct (expression equals 0)

transcription_corrections: Group-2 bracket mean 1′24″51 covers Sep 13 through Nov 3 (7 values), not only Sep 13–21.
Dec 1 and Dec 3 zenith distances and corrections should be read as negative (as written explicitly for Dec 4), by continuity of the correction column.
Dec 16 result is overwritten and illegible ('8 4?.00'); the arithmetic gives 8′38.40.
Side-table entry for Aug 28 is +9.91 (the final digit is overwritten), consistent with the interpolated values.
